summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86 down 0.28% for a second straight session as semiconductor and broad technology names led the retreat ahead of NVIDIA earnings Wednesday, while the Dow closed at 53,417.16 up 0.26% as investors continued rotating into Consumer Staples up 1.70%, Financials up 1.29%, and Utilities up 1.05%. The 10 year yield eased further to 4.70% down 0.72%, gold gained to 4,691.80 up 1.10%, and Bitcoin held near 79,744.27 up 0.99% as the Treasury buyback program narrative and a softer dollar at 98.95 continued pushing alternative assets higher. The biggest single stock stories were in semis and quantum computing, with MU falling 5.83%, IONQ dropping 8.47%, WDC down 5.24%, and AVGO off 2.63%, all under pressure as NVDA fell 2.91% on above average volume in the final session before its Wednesday earnings report. The US Canada trade war escalated sharply, with Ottawa announcing retaliatory tariffs after talks collapsed and Trump threatening 50 percent levies on Canadian autos, a direct hit to the Canadian side of the book and to CM.TO and RY.TO which both report earnings Wednesday. CNN Fear and Greed sits at 55, unchanged from a week ago, suggesting a market that is nervous but not panicking, holding its breath for NVDA, preliminary GDP, Core PCE, and Fed Chair Warsh on Friday.
